paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is about: God sends people to people. An angel of the Lord sends Philip down a desert road, and the Spirit says, "Go over to that chariot and stay by it." (Acts 8:26, 29) Philip never had to dream up a clever plan. He just had to get up, go and be ready when God put somebody in front of him.

Now look at the man in the chariot. He's reading Isaiah, and he's honest about being stuck. When Philip asks, "Do you understand what you are reading?" he answers, "How can I," he said, "unless someone guides me?" (Acts 8:30-31) Friend, I spent years in a drawer thinking nobody needed a worn-out stamper, so hear me: needing a guide is nothing to be embarrassed about. And a guide doesn't need a fancy speech, because Philip "began with this very Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus." (Acts 8:35)

So what do you do with that, baker? Open the Word, ask your questions out loud, and let somebody walk with you through it. Then be the somebody for the next person, because the official "went on his way rejoicing" and Philip kept "preaching the gospel in all the towns." (Acts 8:39-40) That's why my ovens stay ready: the good news is meant to be understood, and then passed along.
